name: Nafasi Art Space
known: The director is Lilian Mushi (Nafasi about page).

name: Bangkok Art Biennale
known: Its page lists as board members Thapana Sirivadhanabhakdi, Group CEO of ThaiBev, and Prof.
Apinan Poshyananda, chief executive and artistic director and a former Acting Minister of Culture.
Its chief executive Thapana is a co-founder and pledged support for the 2020 and 2022 editions (The Nation, 12 July 2017).

name: Bangkok Kunsthalle
known: Founded by the art patron Marisa Chearavanont through her organisation Khao Yai Art.
Led by director and curator Stefano Rabolli Pansera, formerly director of Hauser & Wirth St.
Marisa Chearavanont is married to Soopakij Chearavanont, chairman of the Charoen Pokphand (CP) Group, which ArtReview calls Thailand's largest agribusiness (ArtAsiaPacific;
Presented together with its sister site Khao Yai Art Forest, both founded by Marisa Chearavanont.

name: MOCA Bangkok
known: Founded by the telecoms executive Boonchai Bencharongkul.

Boonchai founded and chairs DTAC, which Wikipedia calls Thailand's third-largest mobile phone operator; he partnered with Telenor of Norway and in 2005 he and his three siblings sold most of their shares while he stayed chairman (Wikipedia).
The museum's site presents a founder's message and its mission only.
It presents the founder's message and its mission only.

name: MAIIAM
known: Founded by Jean Michel Beurdeley and Patsri Bunnag (called late by ArtAsiaPacific), with their son Eric Bunnag Booth.

ArtAsiaPacific says Booth acquired works by Montien Boonma at the recommendation of the curator Gridthiya Gaweewong, and names Vasan Sitthiket, Kosit Juntaratip, Araya Rasdjarmrearnsook and Mit Jai Inn among the artists in his collection (ArtAsiaPacific, 1 May 2020).
It names only the Beurdeley-Bunnag family as founders.
Founded by Jean Michel Beurdeley and Eric Bunnag Booth in memory of Chao Chom Iam.

name: Thailand Biennale
known: Artistic directors Arin Rungjang and David Teh, with curators Hera Chan and Marisa Phandharakrajadej (e-flux).

name: Palais de Lomé
known: The director is Sonia Lawson.
Afrik.com says the project is "fortement soutenu par le chef de l'Etat" (strongly backed by the head of state; translation).

name: Alice Yard
known: Run and curated by Sean Leonard, the artist Christopher Cozier, the writer and editor Nicholas Laughlin, the designer Kriston Chen and the artist Shannon Alonzo, with a changing group of collaborators (stated by the space).

name: Bocas Lit Fest
known: Founded by Marina Salandy-Brown, now board president.
Nicholas Laughlin is festival and programme director (stated by the space).

2012 to 2023: the National Gas Company (NGC), the state-owned gas company, was title sponsor for 12 years, committing in three-year blocks; it funded 2024 only in part and gave nothing in 2025 (Salandy-Brown, festival founder, 2025).

name: B7L9 Art Centre
known: The Art Newspaper (Tim Cornwell, 22 March 2019) reported the opening and the inaugural exhibition "Climbing through the Tide", curated by Başak Şenova, with 50 artists from 21 countries.
Kamel Lazaar is its founder and Lina Lazaar its president (foundation site).
This is the founder's own banking history, not a funder of the centre.
The parent Kamel Lazaar Foundation names 18 partners and funders on an undated page and its founders and staff; no board.

name: B7L9 Art Centre (Kamel Lazaar Foundation)
known: The Art Newspaper (Tim Cornwell, 22 March 2019) reported the opening and the inaugural exhibition "Climbing through the Tide", curated by Başak Şenova, with 50 artists from 21 countries.
Kamel Lazaar is its founder and Lina Lazaar its president (foundation site).
This is the founder's own banking history, not a funder of the centre.

name: Le 32Bis
known: Camille Lévy was artistic director at that time (Managers, 17 February 2022).
In 2026 La Presse describes Hela Djebbi as curator and director.
Kapitalis calls Yosr Ben Ammar and Mehdi Ben Cheikh the two gallery directors (Kapitalis, Fawz Ben Ali, 9 June 2015).
